errors.discriminating_probe: Ask only for the three subinterval widths from the same table; correct widths with a wrong sum points away from BC-MIS-06001.
errors.name: Uniform width applied to a nonuniform partition
non_conceptual_causes: read the first two table inputs, saw one gap, and reused it for the rest
subtracted consecutive inputs correctly but copied one difference twice
reused the layout of a previous uniform partition problem without rereading the inputs
errors.observed_behavior: The response multiplies every tabulated value by one common width although the table inputs are unevenly spaced.
errors.scoring_consequence: The form point is lost because more than one of the six factors is incorrect, and the answer point is lost with it.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask for the left sum and the right sum on the same table and see whether the student can produce both on request.
errors.name: Endpoint opposite the one requested used in the Riemann sum
non_conceptual_causes: read past the word left or right in the stem
started the sum at the first table row out of habit and never checked which endpoints that uses
errors.observed_behavior: A completely correct Riemann sum is built with left endpoints when right endpoints were requested, or the reverse.
errors.scoring_consequence: A completely correct sum of the wrong type earns one of the two remaining points in 2023 and the form point only in 2025 (sg-23:3, sg-25:13).

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask for the units of one term of the sum; rate units alone indicate BC-MIS-06001 rather than a transcription loss.
errors.name: Riemann sum reported as a sum of function values
non_conceptual_causes: copied the table row into the calculator as a list and added it
wrote the widths on scratch paper and never transferred them into the displayed expression
errors.observed_behavior: The response adds the tabulated rate values without multiplying each by a subinterval width.
errors.scoring_consequence: Neither the form point nor the answer point is earned because no products appear.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask for the area of one trapezoid alone; a correct single trapezoid points to a copying loss rather than BC-MIS-06004.
errors.name: Trapezoidal sum with the factor of one half applied to only one term
non_conceptual_causes: factored one half out front, then reapplied it to the first term as well
dropped the factor while recopying the expression onto the next line
errors.observed_behavior: One or two trapezoid terms are halved and the remaining term is not.
errors.scoring_consequence: At least one of the six factors is incorrect, so the form point may survive but the answer point is lost (sg-25:13).

errors.discriminating_probe: Supply a rate that decreases on part of the interval and increases on the rest and ask whether a direction can be decided at all.
errors.name: Over or under estimate claimed without reference to the behaviour of the function
non_conceptual_causes: stopped writing after the numerical answer when the part was the last one attempted
stated the direction from a remembered table of cases without rereading the given behaviour
errors.observed_behavior: The response asserts that an approximation is an underestimate or an overestimate but cites no monotonicity or concavity evidence.
errors.scoring_consequence: The justification point is not earned even when the direction stated is correct.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask the student to draw one rectangle over an increasing arc and say whether it sits above or below the curve.
errors.name: Under and over estimate directions interchanged for a monotone integrand
non_conceptual_causes: recalled the memorised pairing of left with under and stated its opposite
read the graph as decreasing because the axis scale runs downward
errors.observed_behavior: A left sum is called an overestimate for an increasing function, or a right sum an underestimate.
errors.scoring_consequence: The justification point is lost and the answer point with it when the direction is part of the answer.

errors.discriminating_probe: Give an increasing concave down rate and ask for the direction of the trapezoidal estimate; a correct answer there separates a rule mix from BC-MIS-05020.
errors.name: Trapezoidal direction decided from monotonicity instead of concavity
non_conceptual_causes: applied the rectangle rule to a trapezoid because both were learned in the same part
read concave down off the graph but wrote increasing in the justification
errors.observed_behavior: The response argues that a trapezoidal sum overestimates because the function is increasing.
errors.scoring_consequence: The justification point is not earned because the stated reason does not support the conclusion.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask what the plotted curve is called in the stem before any feature is located.
errors.name: Graph of the integrand treated as the graph of the accumulation function
non_conceptual_causes: read the label on the plotted curve as g because g is the letter the part asks about
answered from the previous part, which did ask about features of f
errors.observed_behavior: Extrema or inflection points of g are read directly off the visible extrema and inflection points of the plotted curve.
errors.scoring_consequence: Both the answer and the reason points of the part are lost, and any extra declared input costs both points (sg-25:17).

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask separately where g has extrema and where g has inflection points on the same graph and compare the two lists.
errors.name: Inflection points of an accumulation function placed where the integrand crosses the axis
non_conceptual_causes: carried the zeros found for the extrema part straight into the inflection part
located the turning points of f correctly on scratch work and copied the wrong list into the answer
errors.observed_behavior: The response reports inflection points of g at the zeros of f rather than at the turning points of f.
errors.scoring_consequence: The answer point is not earned, and an extra declared input forfeits the reason point as well (sg-25:17).

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask what feature of the plotted curve makes the claim true; a correct feature named on request points away from BC-MIS-01010.
errors.name: Reason for a feature of the accumulation function phrased only in terms of g
non_conceptual_causes: restated the definition because the justification line was written last and quickly
cited the graph in scratch work and wrote only the conclusion on the answer page
errors.observed_behavior: The response says that g has an inflection point because g changes concavity, without tying the claim to the given graph of f.
errors.scoring_consequence: The answer point is earned but the reason point is not, because the reason must be tied to the given graph of f (sg-25:17).

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask for the complete candidate list on its own, before any values are compared.
errors.name: Candidates comparison left incomplete
non_conceptual_causes: found the critical inputs and listed only those, leaving the endpoints on scratch paper
miscounted the sign changes and stopped the table one row early
errors.observed_behavior: A candidates table omits an endpoint or a critical input, or includes an input that is neither.
errors.scoring_consequence: The justification point requires evaluations or reasoning at every critical input and both endpoints and no others (sg-25:19).

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask for the area of the semicircular piece alone before the integral is assembled.
errors.name: Semicircular region given the area of a full circle
non_conceptual_causes: wrote the circle area formula from memory and never halved it
read the radius off the figure as the diameter
halved the area in the working and copied the unhalved line into the integral
errors.observed_behavior: The area of a semicircular piece of the region is computed as pi times the radius squared.
errors.scoring_consequence: The value point for that integral is lost.
errors.single_cause_note: Only one conceptual cause is plausible, since the rest of the region is handled correctly and the departure is confined to the recalled area formula.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask for the sign of the integral before any number is computed.
errors.name: Regions below the axis added as positive area
non_conceptual_causes: added the pieces on the calculator as magnitudes and never reinstated the sign
read the region below the axis as above it because the figure is shaded on both sides
errors.observed_behavior: Every piece of the region is added with a positive sign, so a signed integral is reported as a plain area.
errors.scoring_consequence: The value point is lost, and any later part that imports the value inherits the error.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask what the integral by itself measures before the value at the later input is requested.
errors.name: Initial condition omitted from a net change computation
non_conceptual_causes: the initial value is stated in the stem several parts earlier and was not carried forward
wrote the sum on scratch paper and transferred only the integral to the answer
errors.observed_behavior: The definite integral of the rate is reported as the value of the quantity at the later input.
errors.scoring_consequence: The initial condition point is not earned; the response that presents only the integral value does not earn it (sg-24:4).

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask for the units of the reported answer; rate units name an average value and accumulated units name a total.
errors.name: Integral reported without the division in an average value
non_conceptual_causes: computed the integral on the calculator and reported the display without the division
took the interval length to be one from a previous part where it was
errors.observed_behavior: The definite integral is presented as the average value with no division by the length of the interval.
errors.scoring_consequence: The average value formula point is lost; a correct integral together with the correct quotient value earns both points even when the linkage is unclear (sg-25:3).

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask for the two u limits explicitly before the antiderivative is evaluated.
errors.name: Original limits of integration kept after a substitution
non_conceptual_causes: converted the limits on scratch paper and substituted from the printed stem instead
wrote the antiderivative in u and stopped before the back substitution when time ran short
errors.observed_behavior: The antiderivative is written in the substituted variable and the original x limits are substituted into it.
errors.scoring_consequence: The response is not eligible for the answer point even when the numerical value is correct (sg-23:17, sg-23:16).

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask the student to differentiate the reported antiderivative and compare it with the integrand.
errors.name: Constant factor from the differential dropped
non_conceptual_causes: solved du for dx correctly and then dropped the reciprocal while recopying
took the inner derivative to be one because the inner expression is linear
errors.observed_behavior: The substitution is carried out without the reciprocal constant that du introduces.
errors.scoring_consequence: The antiderivative point is lost and the value point with it.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask the student to write du and point to it inside the integrand.
errors.name: Substitution attempted when the inner derivative is absent
non_conceptual_causes: matched the composite against a worked example with the same outer function
wrote du but never compared it with the factors actually present in the integrand
errors.observed_behavior: A composite is substituted although no constant multiple of the derivative of the inner expression appears in the integrand.
errors.scoring_consequence: The setup point for the technique is not earned and the work does not lead to the antiderivative.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask the student to differentiate the proposed answer and compare it with the integrand.
errors.name: Factors of a product antidifferentiated separately
non_conceptual_causes: carried the term by term habit over from the sum rule practised immediately before
began parts on scratch paper and copied the first line of the wrong attempt
errors.observed_behavior: The response antidifferentiates each factor of a product and multiplies the results.
errors.scoring_consequence: Neither the u and dv point nor the expression point is earned (sg-23:18, sg-24:18).

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask the student to derive the formula from the product rule and compare with the line they wrote.
errors.name: Minus sign dropped in the integration by parts expression
non_conceptual_causes: recalled the parts formula with the sign of the product rule instead
wrote the minus on the first line and lost it when the second integral was moved across
errors.observed_behavior: The response writes u times v plus the integral of v du.
errors.scoring_consequence: The expression point is not earned, and the answer point depends on it (sg-23:18).
errors.single_cause_note: Only one conceptual cause is plausible, since the response otherwise shows a correct choice of u and dv and the sign is the single departure.

errors.discriminating_probe: Give a convergent and a divergent integral from the same family and ask which converges and why.
errors.name: Value reported for a divergent improper integral
non_conceptual_causes: substituted the infinite limit directly into the antiderivative instead of taking a limit
evaluated the limit of the wrong branch after a sign slip in the antiderivative
errors.observed_behavior: The response produces a finite number although the limit is infinite or fails to exist.
errors.scoring_consequence: The answer point is not earned because the required conclusion is a statement of divergence.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask the student to compare the two degrees before any decomposition is written.
errors.name: Improper rational integrand decomposed without a preliminary division
non_conceptual_causes: began decomposing as soon as the denominator factored, without comparing degrees
read the numerator degree off the leading term of an unexpanded product
errors.observed_behavior: A rational integrand whose numerator degree is at least the denominator degree is split into partial fractions directly.
errors.scoring_consequence: The decomposition cannot be solved consistently and the antiderivative point is not earned.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask for the derivative of the upper limit on its own first.
errors.name: Chain rule factor omitted when the upper limit is a function of x
non_conceptual_causes: applied the form practised with a bare x upper limit without rereading this one
computed the derivative of the upper limit on scratch paper and left it out of the final line
errors.observed_behavior: The derivative of an accumulation function with a composite upper limit is reported as the integrand at that limit with no extra factor.
errors.scoring_consequence: The answer point is not earned even though the theorem point may be (sg-24:15).

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask which letter is the independent variable of the accumulation function and which is the variable of integration.
errors.name: Variable of integration substituted in place of the upper limit
non_conceptual_causes: copied the integrand from the stem, where it is written in t, and never renamed it
answered in t because the previous part asked for a value in t
errors.observed_behavior: The response evaluates the integrand at the dummy variable or leaves the answer in terms of t.
errors.scoring_consequence: The answer point is not earned because the derivative is not expressed in the independent variable.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask the student to name the starting and ending inputs and the units of one term before rewriting the sentence.
errors.name: Interpretation of a definite integral omits the interval or the units
non_conceptual_causes: wrote the sentence in abbreviated form after the numerical work filled the space
took the units from the integrand row of the table rather than from the product
errors.observed_behavior: The response names the accumulated quantity but not the interval over which it accumulates, or gives the units of the rate.
errors.scoring_consequence: The interpretation point requires both the accumulated quantity with units and the interval, so it is not earned (sg-23:2).

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask what changes in the sentence when the leading fraction is removed.
errors.name: Average value expression interpreted as a total
non_conceptual_causes: read past the leading fraction in the displayed expression
interpreted the expression from the previous part, which was a plain integral
errors.observed_behavior: A displayed average value expression is described as the total amount accumulated over the interval.
errors.scoring_consequence: The interpretation point is not earned because the description must say average over the interval (sg-24:3).

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask where the integrand is continuous before the integral is set up.
errors.name: Integral split at a discontinuity omitted
non_conceptual_causes: read only the first branch of the piecewise definition
noticed the jump and split the interval on scratch paper but antidifferentiated the single expression on the answer page
errors.observed_behavior: A function with a jump on the interval of integration is antidifferentiated as a single expression across the jump.
errors.scoring_consequence: The value point is lost because the antiderivative used is not valid across the whole interval.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask for the value of the integrand at one input and compare it with a hand estimate; agreement rules the mode setting out.
errors.name: Calculator left in degree mode for a trigonometric integrand
non_conceptual_causes: calculator left in degree mode from earlier use and never reset
mode changed by a memory reset or a borrowed calculator and not checked before the first evaluation
the trigonometric value was entered in a second calculator window whose mode differs from the first
errors.observed_behavior: Numerical values of an integral or of a rate involving a trigonometric function are computed in degree mode.
errors.scoring_consequence: The first point that the value would otherwise earn is not earned, and the response remains eligible for subsequent points (sg-23:4).
errors.single_cause_note: No internal misconception is plausible here, since the same student produces correct radian work by hand; the behaviour is a tool state, so the alternatives below are all non conceptual.
